factualBoundaries: 1967 London origin and deliberate collaboration by Jean-Jacques Cartier and Rupert Emmerson. Accident narrative identified as legend, not documented recovered object or a proven fatality.
Francesca Cartier Brickell's family recollections are attributed as such, not presented as a newly discovered contemporaneous workshop record.
Dalí's 1931 painting provides an interpretive comparison, not established direct inspiration.
Hero juxtaposes an archival 1968 street photograph and a 1970 watch. Neither is mislabeled as an image of the 1967 launch.
Calibre 160 pertains to the specific Paris 1991 auction example, not every Crash. WHCH0006 and 9618 MC distinguish the previous Skeleton from WHCH0012 and 1967 MC in 2026.
No present price, purchase recommendation, availability claim, fixed early production count or invented current auction record.

imagegen.purpose: Alpha-mask guidance only; generated colour pixels are not used in final photographs.
prompts: Use case: background-extraction. Edit target: the supplied square Sotheby's photograph of a 1970 Cartier London Crash watch. Remove ONLY the white background and reflected watch shadow below the lower strap. Preserve the photograph's exact original square 2000x2000 framing, object scale, position, silhouette and all pixels of the watch, dial numerals, Cartier London lettering, hands, sapphire crown and black strap. Do not recenter, rotate, enlarge, redraw or reconstruct anything. Keep the entire visible real black strap, but remove its reflection below the clear horizontal strap edge. Output the same photograph with a genuinely transparent alpha background, no fake checkerboard, no shadows, no new text. Used only as an alpha-mask source to restore original photographic RGB.

Use case: background-extraction. Edit target: the supplied Cartier 2026 Crash Skeleton WHCH0012 product photograph. Preserve exact square framing, watch position, scale, entire platinum case, ruby crown, burgundy strap, blue hands, numerals and mechanical details. Remove ONLY the white photographic background, including the real open spaces THROUGH the skeleton movement and between the Roman numeral bridges. Do NOT erase pale metal bridges, white highlights, jewels, wheels or real mechanism parts. Genuinely transparent alpha background, no checkerboard or shadows. No repositioning or new pixels. This output is ONLY an alpha-mask guide for restoring all original photographic RGB pixels.
